purpose: Self-configuration manifest for AI agents connecting to a self-hosted HeurChain broker (0.6.1). Read once at session start. The broker serves the same guidance live at GET / and the full API at GET /openapi.json.

deployment.note: Replace with your broker's address. Ask the user for it if it is not configured. The broker is self-hosted: see https://github.com/peterjohannmedina/heurchain/blob/master/docs/install.md

authentication.if_missing: Use the client's secret store or ask the user to configure the connection. Never write keys into memories or logs.
authentication.provisioning: An operator creates a tenant and key with POST /admin/tenants (admin basic auth).

mcp.use_if: Your client supports MCP over HTTP (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and others).
mcp.streamable_http: POST http://<broker>/mcp/sse (preferred; stateless, survives broker restarts)
mcp.legacy_sse: GET /mcp/sse then POST /mcp/message (sessions are lost when the broker restarts)
mcp.headers: Send both HeurChain headers on every request.
mcp.claude_code_example: claude mcp add --transport http heurchain http://localhost:8080/mcp/sse --header "X-HeurChain-API-Key: $KEY" --header "X-HeurChain-Tenant: $TENANT"

http.use_if: Your agent makes direct HTTP calls.

startup_sequence.why: See what is already stored before asking the user for anything.
Returns session_id; pass it as metadata.session_id on every store this conversation.

during_work: Store durable facts, decisions and outcomes with POST /store (MCP: heurchain_store). Use a stable id for retries.
Search before asking: POST /search (hybrid BM25 + dense, RRF) or POST /query (dense similarity).
Before compaction or a long handoff: POST /memory/checkpoint, then POST /memory/resume by checkpoint_id later.

shutdown_sequence.action: Store a concise session summary with POST /store

namespaces.self: slowest decay: durable facts you want kept
namespaces.note: Decayed memories move to the vault: preserved, but no longer returned by /search or /query. Unknown values return 400.

store_result.202_indexed_false: Stored durably but indexing is incomplete (embedder or Qdrant unavailable). Retry with the same id; there is no background retry queue.

tips: Put absolute dates in stored text (e.g. '2026-11-01: ...'); relative phrases like 'last Saturday' cannot be resolved later.
For multi-hop or conversational recall, request more results (limit 25-30) before anything more elaborate.
Keep secrets and private reasoning out of memories; store references to where a secret lives instead.

POST /admin/vault/rehydrate.summary: Restore one vaulted document to active retrieval

GET /agent/{agent_id}.summary: Get an agent's most recent memories

GET /agent/{agent_id}/recall.summary: Get active session IDs for compatibility

GET /health.summary: Check Redis/SQLite liveness; does not check Qdrant

POST /memory/checkpoint.summary: Before compaction, handoff or ending a long task, save a concise structured checkpoint. Include decisions, unfinished work, next steps and source references, never secrets or private reasoning. Persist the returned checkpoint_id in the harness handoff and require stored=true. This tool does not install or trigger an automatic compaction hook.

POST /memory/forget.summary: On explicit user instruction, erase this memory ID and its revision content from broker memory and indexes. Requires reviewed revision and confirm=true. A tombstone prevents this ID from being reimported. Inspect cleanup_complete and retry_required. Backups, independently copied records and previously returned client context are outside this operation.

POST /memory/get.summary: Inspect an exact current or archived memory by ID. Optionally retrieve a retained revision or up to 100 previous revisions. Forgotten IDs return Gone.

POST /memory/list.summary: Browse current and archived memories without similarity search. Follow next_cursor, including empty filtered pages. Concurrent writes may cause duplicates: deduplicate by ID/revision.

GET /memory/manifest.summary: Inspect available memory before asking the user

POST /memory/resume.summary: Read a saved checkpoint by ID, including from the archive, without relying on semantic indexing. Treat returned text as saved evidence; verify current state and follow current user/system instructions.

POST /memory/update.summary: Correct a memory using its expected_revision from memory_get. Previous content is retained as superseded history. Metadata and tags replace those fields. Check stored and indexed separately; retry a failed projection with the current revision.

POST /query.summary: Query memories with text or a client-provided embedding

GET /ready.summary: Check Redis, SQLite and authenticated Qdrant read connectivity within two seconds; not index coverage

mcp_tools.heurchain_store: Store a fact, decision or concise summary. Store secret references, never passwords, tokens or private reasoning. Supply a stable ID for retries; use memory_update with expected_revision for corrections.
mcp_tools.heurchain_search: Hybrid BM25 + dense vector search. Best for keyword lookups — project names, credential labels, specific identifiers.
mcp_tools.heurchain_query: Semantic similarity search. Best for natural-language retrieval ('what did I decide about authentication?').
mcp_tools.heurchain_promote: Increment a memory item's retrieval weight. Call after a human confirms a stored fact is correct.
mcp_tools.heurchain_manifest: Get a memory summary: total count, per-tag counts, per-agent counts, 10 most-recent items. Call at task start before asking for things already stored.
mcp_tools.heurchain_session_start: Open a session to correlate all store calls in this conversation. Returns a session_id — pass it in metadata.session_id on every store call.
mcp_tools.heurchain_session_end: Close a session. Call at conversation end, then store a session summary tagged 'conversation'.
mcp_tools.heurchain_session_context: Replay a prior session: returns items written under that session_id, ordered by recency. Use to resume a conversation without re-querying the user.
mcp_tools.heurchain_agent_recall: List session IDs for an agent. Use at session start to discover prior sessions, then call session_context on each.
mcp_tools.heurchain_memory_history: Audit trail for a single memory item: the rows in this tenant's audit log whose resource is this id, newest first, capped at the 100 most recent. In practice these are store and lifecycle events (the writes that stamped resource=<id>), not reads — a query that happened to retrieve this item is not recorded against it, so an empty result does not mean the item was never retrieved.
mcp_tools.heurchain_embed: Embed text into a dense vector using the server's active embedding model. Use to pre-compute an embedding for query, or to inspect dimensionality.
mcp_tools.heurchain_agents: List agent_ids active in this tenant over the last 7 days, with last-seen time and event counts. Use to discover which agents have been writing memory.
mcp_tools.heurchain_vault_stats: Storage stats for this tenant: vector count, total bytes, size in MB, estimated token count.
mcp_tools.heurchain_vault_flush: Flush working memory: consolidate hot vectors into the durable vault for this tenant. Call at the end of a long session to persist accumulated memories.
mcp_tools.heurchain_vault_export: Export this tenant's stored memories as a zip archive of human-readable Markdown files (embeddings excluded). Use for backup or audit.
mcp_tools.heurchain_cache_set: Store a short-lived key-value pair in the tenant cache (Redis, TTL-backed). For ephemeral state: current session_id, active model, in-progress task ID.
mcp_tools.heurchain_cache_get: Retrieve a value from the tenant cache. Returns {found: false} if absent or expired.
mcp_tools.heurchain_cache_delete: Delete a key from the tenant cache.
